verdict.rationale: NVIDIA's first-party H200 page documents LLM inference with specific benchmarks (Llama2 70B 1.9X, GPT-3 175B 1.6X, up to 2X over H100). Serving-stack evidence is thin: TensorRT-LLM is named only generically for data-center DeepSeek deployments, and NIM via AI Enterprise is tied to the H200 NVL bundle, not the SXM part. Missing for 10: any documented FP8/FP4 low-precision format support, explicit H200-specific TensorRT-LLM support, vLLM or llama.cpp support, and independent hands-on corroboration of the inference stack.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, this GPU has a documented LLM inference story — low-precision formats (FP8/FP4) and supported serving stacks (TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, ROCm, llama.cpp) for this part

citations.quote: The H200 boosts inference speed by up to 2X compared to H100 GPUs when handling LLMs like Llama2.
DeepSeek models can be optimized for performance using TensorRT-LLM for data center deployments.
NVIDIA AI Enterprise includes NVIDIA NIM™, a set of easy-to-use microservices designed to speed up enterprise generative AI deployment.
